title: Live database security posture is below autonomy prerequisite
risk_statement: If consequential AI/VE capabilities are activated against the current live database before RLS/grant/search-path and migration prerequisites are reconciled, unauthorized access or ungoverned execution could occur.
existing_controls: Production autonomy is blocked; repository hardening exists only as isolated evidence; live posture is read-only monitored.
treatment: Avoid production VE/provider autonomy on the live database; open a separate authorized hardening lane with ordered migration delta, backup/recovery readiness, isolated validation and post-deployment advisor/catalog verification.
review_trigger: Any proposed production autonomy or live migration; security-advisor/RLS/grant change

title: External model/provider data cost or behavior change
risk_statement: Provider requests can expose bounded conversation/context data, incur cost, fail, time out or change model behavior/rates; production routing through the stronger governed wrapper is not established.
existing_controls: Provider disabled by default; guarded isolated live smoke; store=false adapter behavior; governed wrapper has preflight/exposure/reservation/replay controls in isolated verification.
treatment: Keep production provider enablement explicit; reconcile ordinary assistant and governed-provider paths before consequential production use; reassess model/rate/terms/data use and preserve bounded retries/cost authority.
review_trigger: Provider/model/rate-card/terms change; production enablement; new data class; incident

title: Premature Virtual Employee authority or excessive agency
risk_statement: Activating agents or external adapters before live identity, grants, authorization, budget, recovery and database security controls are deployed could create unauthorized or irrecoverable actions.
existing_controls: Foundry broker is isolated/C0-C2 only; C3/C4 fail closed; live cm_agent count is zero; no production external adapter is accepted.
treatment: Continue to block live VE activation; require live hardening, explicit least-privilege identities/grants, adapter-specific testing, rollback/recovery, budget authority and human approval before consequential capability.
review_trigger: Agent activation; capability/grant change; external adapter addition; authority ceiling increase

title: Duplicate orphaned or stale delegated work
risk_statement: Without effective lease fencing and recovery, concurrent or crashed workers could duplicate work, silently lose ownership, or act after authority has moved to another worker.
existing_controls: Lease token/epoch fencing, bounded duration, reclaim, stale-owner rejection, exhaustion and independent-connection contention tests are isolated verified; no worker is active.
treatment: Before worker activation, benchmark realistic workload/connection-pool occupancy and define renewal/retry/crash recovery plus terminal monitoring/cleanup; keep lease ownership separate from execution authority.
review_trigger: Worker implementation; production deployment; retry/renewal policy change; contention/load evidence

title: Ungoverned or low-quality memory RAG and knowledge data
risk_statement: Future ingestion/retrieval could propagate incorrect, poisoned, sensitive, stale or improperly authorized memory/knowledge into AI decisions if provenance, quality, retention and access controls are incomplete.
existing_controls: Schema and vector capability exist; current observed material memory/knowledge tables are empty; AIMS data/risk contracts require provenance and review before activation.
treatment: Do not activate production ingestion/RAG from this schema until data classes, acquisition authority, lineage, quality criteria, retention/access rules, poisoning defenses and system-specific impact assessment are controlled and tested.

title: Supplier concentration and continuity dependency
risk_statement: Material dependence on OpenAI, Supabase, GitHub and the package ecosystem can create availability, terms, data-flow, pricing, supply-chain or exit risk where tested substitutes and recovery plans are incomplete.
existing_controls: Provider can be disabled; PostgreSQL architecture is portable in principle; git/lockfile provenance exists; supplier inventory records unknowns instead of assuming assurance.
treatment: Complete supplier due diligence/data-flow/terms evidence; test database export/restore and continuity paths; define provider substitution triggers and package-supply-chain response.
review_trigger: Supplier outage/incident; terms/subprocessor/region/model change; cost shock; exit/restore test

title: Evidence drift or false deployment/compliance claims
risk_statement: Repository implementation, isolated tests, live schema and operating evidence can diverge; if states are collapsed, CoMind could overstate deployment, control effectiveness or ISO readiness.
existing_controls: Evidence-state vocabulary, GOV-002 crosswalk validator, exact-head CI, live read-only snapshots and explicit claim boundaries distinguish design/test/deploy/operation/normative states.
treatment: Keep machine-readable inventory evidence-state checks; refresh live observations after deployment; require exact source/version/date and human approval for certification/conformity claims.
review_trigger: Any deployment; evidence-source change; standard/framework update; audit/certification planning; stale observation

title: Continuity checkpoint capability is not yet accepted on main
risk_statement: Relying on ACP continuity/checkpoint behavior before the parallel ACP lane is merged and exact-head accepted could create false assumptions about recovery, rollover or delegated-work continuity.
existing_controls: Current conversation persistence and Foundry recovery primitives have accepted evidence; the AIMS matrix explicitly treats ACP #84 as parallel work rather than accepted control evidence.
treatment: Do not include ACP #84 as an active inventoried capability until it merges and is reconciled against then-current main; continue using only accepted persistence/recovery evidence.
review_trigger: ACP #84 merge/closure; checkpoint runtime integration; recovery semantics change
